target_customer: Industrial and defense manufacturers and field-service teams paying for AR work instructions and remote assistance
problem: Technicians need expert guidance and up-to-date procedures in the field. Scope AR provides remote AR assistance and WorkLink for authoring and delivering AR instructions.
product_category: Enterprise augmented reality, remote assistance and work instructions

founders.name: David Nedohin
previous_startups: Own consulting firm and technology startups
founders.background_notes: Edmonton based; per a podcast listing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time AR tracking and annotation over live video on tablets and early smartglasses in 2015 required computer vision work on immature hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise and defense customers embed procedures in the platform, but AR vendors such as PTC were large and competitive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: PTC Chalk and TeamViewer Frontline competed in later years; Scope AR persisted independently until sold in 2026.

market_need_then: Enterprises were testing smartglasses for remote expert use in 2014 and 2015, shown by CES 2014 and AWE 2015 demos with Epson hardware.

rebrands.why: Acquired; will operate under the Flatirons Solutions brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within enterprise AR with defense and industrial customers, but no consumer or community brand evidence.

pivots.to: WorkLink AR work instruction platform plus remote assistance
pivots.why: WorkLink introduced in 2017 as a licensable platform for building AR solutions.

outcome_analysis: Scope AR started in 2011 and joined YC in 2015, raised about 15.8 million dollars through a March 2019 Series A, and sold to Flatirons Solutions in June 2026 with terms undisclosed. No shutdown cause exists because the company was acquired. The 15 years from founding to a small, undisclosed exit suggests slow enterprise AR adoption rather than a breakout.
